summary: PJM moves to hold the E-7 show cause proceeding in abeyance for 90 days from August 17, 2026 so it can develop a section 205 filing alongside its co-located load compliance work, with stakeholder sessions and an October 28 advisory vote.
ask: Grant a 90-day abeyance starting August 17, 2026, shorten the answer period to five days, and rule by August 6, 2026.

points.point: PJM seeks a 90-day abeyance because the show cause reforms build on co-located load compliance changes.
points.quote: Many of the changes contemplated in the Large Load Order will build upon compliance changes recently ordered for Co-Located Load in Docket Nos. EL25-49-000, et al.

points.point: PJM expects its section 205 filing in early to mid-November.
points.quote: PJM anticipates submitting that filing by early to mid-November.

points.point: The overlap covers expanded transmission services, study procedures and operational requirements.
points.quote: (1) expansion of new transmission services; (2) study procedures; and (3) operational requirements.

points.point: PJM's planned filing covers study processes with alternative transmission technologies, cost shifting and transparency, flexible load services, and proximate generation study.
points.quote: achieve efficient transmission service application and study processes, including through the consideration of alternative transmission technologies

points.point: PJM schedules stakeholder sessions on July 30, August 18 and September 16, with an advisory vote on October 28, 2026.
points.quote: with the goal of taking an advisory stakeholder vote on the proposal at the meeting of the Members Committee on October 28, 2026

throughLine.text: Asks to defer the E-7 60-day show cause response, tying it to the E-2 co-location compliance order and its Interim NITS service. FERC granted the abeyance on August 14, 2026.
